subject: maths
question: A tank has a mixture of solutions X, Y, and Z in the ratio 5 : 4 : 1. 30 litres of this mixture is drained out, and then 10 litres of solution X and 5 litres of solution Z are added to the tank. If the resultant quantity of solution X is 11 litres more than the resultant quantity of solution Y, find the initial quantity of the mixture in the tank (in litres)?
solution:
**Given:**

Ratio X : Y : Z = 5 : 4 : 1

30 litres mixture drained

Added: X = 10 L, Z = 5 L

Resultant X = Resultant Y + 11 L

Calculations

Initial X = Q × (5/10) = Q × 0.5

Initial Y = Q × (4/10) = Q × 0.4

Initial Z = Q × (1/10) = Q × 0.1

Drained X = 30 × (5/10) = 15 L

Drained Y = 30 × (4/10) = 12 L

Drained Z = 30 × (1/10) = 3 L

Resultant X = Initial X − Drained X + Added X

⇒ Resultant X = Q × 0.5 − 15 + 10 = Q × 0.5 − 5

Resultant Y = Initial Y − Drained Y

⇒ Resultant Y = Q × 0.4 − 12

Resultant Z = Initial Z − Drained Z + Added Z

⇒ Given: Resultant X = Resultant Y + 11

⇒ Q × 0.5 − 5 = (Q × 0.4 − 12) + 11

⇒ Q × 0.5 − 5 = Q × 0.4 − 1

⇒ Q × (0.5 − 0.4) = −1 + 5

⇒ Q × 0.1 = 4

⇒ Q = 4 ÷ 0.1 = 40 litres

**∴ Initial quantity of the mixture = 40 litres.**
